title: SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error)

slides.title: Understanding SFINAE
slides.prompt: SFINAE stands for Substitution Failure Is Not An Error. During overload resolution, if substituting a template parameter with a type fails, the compiler simply ignores that overload instead of throwing a compilation error.

slides.title: SFINAE Utility Helper
slides.prompt: Fill in the missing standard type trait used to conditionally enable function overloads.

slides.title: SFINAE Scope Boundary
slides.prompt: Where does SFINAE apply during the template specialization/overload resolution process?
options: Only in the immediate context of the function signature and template parameter list
In non-templated member functions of ordinary classes
slides.correctAnswer: Only in the immediate context of the function signature and template parameter list

slides.title: enable_if_t Helper Alias (C++14)
slides.prompt: Fill in the C++14 alias template suffix for enable_if.

slides.title: Hard Error vs SFINAE Failure
slides.prompt: What happens if a type substitution error occurs within the function body rather than the signature?
options: A hard compile error occurs because SFINAE only applies to the signature context
The compiler discards the function overload cleanly via SFINAE
The program throws a runtime exception
The compiler substitutes the type with std::void_t
slides.correctAnswer: A hard compile error occurs because SFINAE only applies to the signature context

slides.title: std::void_t Purpose
slides.prompt: What is the primary usage of std::void_t in expression validity testing with SFINAE (C++17)?
options: To map any sequence of valid types to type void for detecting valid expressions
To cast pointers safely across template parameter packs
To force function templates to return no value
To allocate untyped memory during template evaluation
slides.correctAnswer: To map any sequence of valid types to type void for detecting valid expressions

slides.title: std::declval Functionality
slides.prompt: Why is std::declval<T>() useful inside decltype expressions when writing SFINAE traits?
options: It allows referencing member functions of T without needing a constructor call
It instantiates an object of type T on the heap at compile time
It converts rvalue references to lvalue references
It generates default value initializations for primitive types
slides.correctAnswer: It allows referencing member functions of T without needing a constructor call
